stanzas.sanskrit:
स्तम्भे घट्टयतो हिरण्यकशिपोः कर्णौ समाचूर्णय-
-न्नाघूर्णज्जगदण्डकुण्डकुहरो घोरस्तवाभूद्रवः ।
श्रुत्वा यं किल दैत्यराजहृदये पूर्वं कदाऽप्यश्रुतं
कम्पः कश्चन सम्पपात चलितोऽप्यम्भोजभूर्विष्टरात् ॥ २५-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: As Hiranyakashipu struck at the pillar, he heard a terrific sound which was so fierce that it made everything tremble. Hearing this sound which was never heard before, Hiranyakashipu felt an incredible shiver within. Even the lotus born Brahma was shaken from his throne.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
stambhe ghaṭṭayato hiraṇyakaśipoḥ karṇau samācūrṇaya-
-nnāghūrṇajjagadaṇḍakuṇḍakuharo ghorastavābhūdravaḥ |
śrutvā yaṃ kila daityarājahṛdaye pūrvaṃ kadā’pyaśrutaṃ
kampaḥ kaścana sampapāta calito’pyambhojabhūrviṣṭarāt || 25-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दैत्ये दिक्षु विसृष्टचक्षुषि महासंरम्भिणि स्तम्भतः
सम्भूतं न मृगात्मकं न मनुजाकारं वपुस्ते विभो ।
किं किं भीषणमेतदद्भुतमिति व्युद्भ्रान्तचित्तेऽसुरे
विस्फूर्जद्धवलोग्ररोमविकसद्वर्ष्मा समाजृम्भथाः ॥ २५-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hiranyakashipu looked all around in great confusion, from the pillar emerged. Bhagwan’s form which was neither of a beast nor of a human being. Hiranyakashipu in an agitated state of mind wondered as to what this terrific wondrous being might be, Bhagwan expanded into a bigger form.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
daitye dikṣu visṛṣṭacakṣuṣi mahāsaṃrambhiṇi stambhataḥ
sambhūtaṃ na mṛgātmakaṃ na manujākāraṃ vapuste vibho |
kiṃ kiṃ bhīṣaṇametadadbhutamiti vyudbhrāntacitte’sure
visphūrjaddhavalograromavikasadvarṣmā samājṛmbhathāḥ || 25-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तप्तस्वर्णसवर्णघूर्णदतिरूक्षाक्षं सटाकेसर-
-प्रोत्कम्पप्रनिकुम्बिताम्बरमहो जीयात् तवेदं वपुः ।
व्यात्तव्याप्तमहादरीसखमुखं खड्गोग्रवल्गन्महा-
-जिह्वानिर्गमदृश्यमानसुमहादंष्ट्रायुगोड्डामरम् ॥ २५-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan emerged with fierce rolling eyes shining like molten gold, with quivering mane reaching the skies, with a wide open cave like mouth, with a sword like huge tongue rolling out, with a pair of huge fierce teeth.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
taptasvarṇasavarṇaghūrṇadatirūkṣākṣaṃ saṭākesara-
-protkampapranikumbitāmbaramaho jīyāt tavedaṃ vapuḥ |
vyāttavyāptamahādarīsakhamukhaṃ khaḍgogravalganmahā-
-jihvānirgamadṛśyamānasumahādaṃṣṭrāyugoḍḍāmaram || 25-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
उत्सर्पद्वलिभङ्गभीषणहनुं ह्रस्वस्थवीयस्तर-
-ग्रीवं पीवरदोः शतोद्गतनखक्रूरांशुदूरोल्बणम् ।
व्योमोल्लङ्घि घनाघनोपमघनप्रध्वाननिर्धावित-
-स्पर्धालुप्रकरं नमामि भवतस्तन्नारसिंहं वपुः ॥ २५-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s Man-Lion form with chin having folds while roaring, with a short stout neck, with a hundred powerful arms projecting ferocious claws, with terrific roaring voice driving away all the rivals in fright.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
utsarpadvalibhaṅgabhīṣaṇahanuṃ hrasvasthavīyastara-
-grīvaṃ pīvaradoḥ śatodgatanakhakrūrāṃśudūrolbaṇam |
vyomollaṅghi ghanāghanopamaghanapradhvānanirdhāvita-
-spardhāluprakaraṃ namāmi bhavatastannārasiṃhaṃ vapuḥ || 25-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
नूनं विष्णुरयं निहन्म्यमुमिति भ्राम्यद्गदाभीषणं
दैत्येन्द्रं समुपाद्रवन्तमधृथा दोर्भ्यां पृथुभ्याममुम् ।
वीरो निर्गलितोऽथ खड्गफलकौ गृह्णन् विचित्रश्रमान्
व्यावृण्वन् पुनरापपात भुवनग्रासोद्यतं त्वामहो ॥ २५-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hiranyakashipu realised it to be Bhagwan who has come to kill him. Bhagwan held Hiranyakashipu's hands tightly by his stout arms, he slipped himself from the grip and came back rushing towards Bhagwan with the sword and shield.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
nūnaṃ viṣṇurayaṃ nihanmyamumiti bhrāmyadgadābhīṣaṇaṃ
daityendraṃ samupādravantamadhṛthā dorbhyāṃ pṛthubhyāmamum |
vīro nirgalito’tha khaḍgaphalakau gṛhṇan vicitraśramān
vyāvṛṇvan punarāpapāta bhuvanagrāsodyataṃ tvāmaho || 25-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भ्राम्यन्तं दितिजाधमं पुनरपि प्रोद्गृह्य दोर्भ्यां जवात्
द्वारेऽथोरुयुगे निपात्य नखरान् व्युत्खाय वक्षोभुवि ।
निर्भिन्दन्नधिगर्भनिर्भरगलद्रक्ताम्बु बद्धोत्सवं
पायं पायमुदैरयो बहुजगत्संहारिसिंहारवान् ॥ २५-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord in form of Narasimha, half man and half lion, held him by his hand, supported him on his thighs at the doorway, on twilight and tore his chest with his claws and drank the blood oozing out of his body, fiercely roaring strong enough to shatter the universe.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhrāmyantaṃ ditijādhamaṃ punarapi prodgṛhya dorbhyāṃ javāt
dvāre’thoruyuge nipātya nakharān vyutkhāya vakṣobhuvi |
nirbhindannadhigarbhanirbharagaladraktāmbu baddhotsavaṃ
pāyaṃ pāyamudairayo bahujagatsaṃhārisiṃhāravān || 25-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा तं हतमाशु रक्तलहरीसिक्तोन्नमद्वर्ष्मणि
प्रत्युत्पत्य समस्तदैत्यपटलीं चाखाद्यमाने त्वयि ।
भ्राम्यद्भूमि विकम्पिताम्बुधिकुलं व्यालोलशैलोत्करं
प्रोत्सर्पत्खचरं चराचरमहो दुःस्थामवस्थां दधौ ॥ २५-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Pushing away the dead body, Lord Narasimha sprang up with body bathed in blood, started to eat the other asuras, roaring loudly that caused mountains tremble, oceans turbulent, stars and other celestial objects scatter, causing an utter chaos in the universe.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tyaktvā taṃ hatamāśu raktalaharīsiktonnamadvarṣmaṇi
pratyutpatya samastadaityapaṭalīṃ cākhādyamāne tvayi |
bhrāmyadbhūmi vikampitāmbudhikulaṃ vyālolaśailotkaraṃ
protsarpatkhacaraṃ carācaramaho duḥsthāmavasthāṃ dadhau || 25-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तावन्मांसवपाकरालवपुषं घोरान्त्रमालाधरं
त्वां मध्येसभमिद्धरोषमुषितं दुर्वारगुर्वारवम् ।
अभ्येतुं न शशाक कोऽपि भुवने दूरे स्थिता भीरवः
सर्वे शर्वविरिञ्चवासवमुखाः प्रत्येकमस्तोषत ॥ २५-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan was roaring again and again in great fury smeared with flesh and wearing the intestine of Hirnyakashipu as garland. No one dared to approach Bhagwan, and stood far away. Even Shiva, Brahmaa, Indra and others kept at a distance, singing Bhagwan’s praises individually and tried to pacify.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāvanmāṃsavapākarālavapuṣaṃ ghorāntramālādharaṃ
tvāṃ madhyesabhamiddharoṣamuṣitaṃ durvāragurvāravam |
abhyetuṃ na śaśāka ko’pi bhuvane dūre sthitā bhīravaḥ
sarve śarvaviriñcavāsavamukhāḥ pratyekamastoṣata || 25-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भूयोऽप्यक्षतरोषधाम्नि भवति ब्रह्माज्ञया बालके
प्रह्लादे पदयोर्नमत्यपभये कारुण्यभाराकुलः ।
शान्तस्त्वं करमस्य मूर्ध्नि समधाः स्तोत्रैरथोद्गायत-
-स्तस्याकामधियोऽपि तेनिथ वरं लोकाय चानुग्रहम् ॥ २५-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Prahlada, free of fear, went near and prostrated before Bhagwan. On seeing his devotee, his anger reduced, and now becoming soft and kind, touched and blessed the boy with deep compassion. With Bhagwan's touch, Prahlada started to sing in praise of Bhagwan and received boon in favour of the world
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhūyo’pyakṣataroṣadhāmni bhavati brahmājñayā bālake
prahlāde padayornamatyapabhaye kāruṇyabhārākulaḥ |
śāntastvaṃ karamasya mūrdhni samadhāḥ stotrairathodgāyata-
-stasyākāmadhiyo’pi tenitha varaṃ lokāya cānugraham || 25-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवं नाटितरौद्रचेष्टित विभो श्रीतापनीयाभिध-
-श्रुत्यन्तस्फुटगीतसर्वमहिमन्नत्यन्तशुद्धाकृते ।
तत्तादृङ्निखिलोत्तरं पुनरहो कस्त्वां परो लङ्घयेत्
प्रह्लादप्रिय हे मरुत्पुरपते सर्वामयात् पाहि माम् ॥ २५-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Prahalada Priyanae !
Bhattathiri praised Bhagwan who enacted this fierce drama to slay an asura and protect his prime devotee is pure and free from anger. He requests Bhagwan to cure him of his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
evaṃ nāṭitaraudraceṣṭita vibho śrītāpanīyābhidha-
-śrutyantasphuṭagītasarvamahimannatyantaśuddhākṛte |
tattādṛṅnikhilottaraṃ punaraho kastvāṃ paro laṅghayet
prahlādapriya he marutpurapate sarvāmayāt pāhi mām || 25-10 ||
